error: Uses one formula for the other measure
shows: The words have no pictures yet
if_many: Sort ten situations by drawing what is measured: the inside or the edge

error: Adds one length and one width
shows: The edge is not seen going all the way round
if_many: Trace and name four sides; write l + w + l + w

error: Finds a side from an area by subtracting, adding, or multiplying the two numbers given
shows: The formula is not seen as a multiplication with a missing factor
example: "35 square feet, 5 wide, so 30 long" (it is 7)
if_many: Rows of 5 on grid paper until the 35 squares are used

error: From a perimeter, takes off one side, or does not halve
shows: One pair of sides is counted
source: IM lesson 17 (one side taken off); not halving is from memory
example: "44 feet of fence, 14 long, so 30 wide" (it is 8)

error: Wrong unit: "40 feet" for an area
shows: Squares and lengths are not told apart
example: "A rug 9 feet by 3 feet has an area of 27 feet"
if_many: Eight answers with no units: write feet or square feet on each

error: Counts the squares along the edge, not the unit sides
shows: The edge is not yet seen as unit lengths
source: From memory; teaching move Prog. p. 108 (102)
if_many: Tick and number each unit side along the edge, then count the ticks

error: Reads "times as many" as "more than": 5 times as many as 3 is 8
shows: Comparing still means adding on, as in grade 2
example: "8 times as many as 3 is 11", a 3-strip and a strip of 3 and 8, beside eight copies of the 3-strip (24)
if_many: Build both with cubes, "8 more than 3" and "8 times as many as 3"; say which is which

error: Multiplies because the problem says "times", when the smaller amount or the number of times is unknown
shows: A key word is followed in place of the situation
example: "Jo has 12 shells. That is 2 times as many as Max has. Max has 24", beside 6
if_many: Before any numbers: "who has more?" Mark the longer strip; the answer must fit it

error: Swaps the roles: says the smaller amount is so many times as many as the larger
shows: Lost track of which number is the multiplier
example: "12 is 4 times as many as 3" written as 3 = 4 × 12, beside 12 = 4 × 3
if_many: Point to the longer strip first: "which amount is bigger?"; the bigger amount stands alone in the equation

error: Draws the first amount and then that many more copies, or counts both amounts together
shows: "Times as many" taken as copies added on top
source: Partly IM lesson 2; the rest from memory
example: "4 times as many as 3" drawn as a 3-strip with four more 3-strips after it (15), beside four copies (12)
if_many: Count the copies aloud, starting with the first strip as copy one

error: First idea, not an error: "3 times more than 4" could mean 12 or 16
shows: The phrase is unclear in everyday English
example: "3 times more than 4 dollars": is it 12 or 16? A talk, not a correction
if_many: Not marked. Our problems say "times as much"

shows: Solves the part that was easy to see
example: "Lena has 40 dollars. Omar has 2 times as much. How much do they have together? 80", beside 120
if_many: Underline the question; after solving, read the question again and ask "is that what I found?"

error: Gives an answer with no equation, or a letter that stands for nothing named
shows: The equation is seen as extra, not as the plan
example: An answer alone, 33, beside "s = 4 × 6 + 9, s is all the stickers, s = 33"
if_many: Say what the letter stands for, in words, before any numbers are written

error: Works a two-step equation left to right: 10 + 3 × 3 = 39
shows: Order of operations from grade 3 is not firm
if_many: Write the two steps as two equations for a week, then join them
